//: Pyright configuration for GPT-Register-Tool.
Pyright has no per-directory rule overrides (an `overrides` block is not a
recognised setting), so the split this repo actually relies on is:
1. `scripts/pyright_ratchet.py` freezes the error count per file and fails
on growth. That ratchet -- not this file -- is the gate. Existing debt
(mostly `reportOptionalMemberAccess` on dict guards, and the mock/
Playwright attribute access that `tests/` cannot avoid) is retired file
by file, each with its own tests.
2. This file only sets the checking mode and excludes trees whose code the
project does not own (vendored, generated, runtime data, build output).
Type-checking `sms_tool/upi_link/_vendor/` or `dist/` would report
thousands of errors in third-party code.
`typeCheckingMode: basic` is deliberate. `standard`/`strict` add the
`reportUnknown*` families, which on a codebase whose primary data shape is
`Any`-heavy JSON payloads produce noise proportional to payload nesting
rather than to defect risk.
The second `executionEnvironment` mirrors the `sys.path` the extractor
tests build themselves: `services/protocol-payment` puts `common` on the
path as a top-level package, and the extractor folders (`kakao`, `momo`)
are not packages at all. Without it pyright reports those imports as
unresolvable even though the tests import them fine. Note that a matching
execution environment *replaces* the top-level `extraPaths`, so `"."` has
to be repeated there.
See docs/current/typing.md for the ratchet workflow.
